Name: Prasanna Bhalerao
Question: Why Inheritance tax is needed in India? Will it stop Adani and Ambani?
Answer: One ultra-stupid person, probably who has gone senile, has proposed a cock-and-bull idea and the whole nation is talking about it one way or another. Inheritance Tax is nothing less than taxing the dead person’s estate because using his ingenuity and methods to grow wealth, s/he is being penalised. For the record, India did have an Inheritance Tax till 1985. Rajeev Gandhi and his then FM V P Singh abolished it. It is a very stupid idea. And NO for part 2 - it won’t stop Adani or Ambani. The more comments that I am reading here supporting this draconian tax, the more I am convinced that voting for BJP/Modi is the right choice (not that I had any doubts). In response to Vignesh Vijay … I said 40% tax rate because that is what the tax rate that is being discussed in informal channels. But the tax rate is not the issue. Even if it is 1% or 2%, it is draconian. That said, any rate below 20%, the effort to collect the tax, the paperwork, the valuation system, and all that jazz makes it inefficient and not worthwhile. People claim to various things without referring to history and studying implications. People think - Yeah! These Ambanis and Adanis are bastards who amassed wealth by stealing, avoiding taxes, looting the people, illegal favours from the government, etc. Now let us loot them back by levying some retrograde tax. Let us start with Inheritance tax. I am sorry - Robinhoodism may look and feel nice but it still has “hoodism” inside the word. This is communism. You love it? Move to Cuba, Venezuela, or wherever the state have unlimited power. Now a bit of this tax history in India: Estate duty meant taxing the entirety of an individual's property value at the time of their passing, with the tax obligation triggered upon transfer to heirs. This duty applied to real estate and movable assets within or outside India. However, the tax faced public Opposition due to its steep rates, reaching up to 85 per cent for properties valued over Rs 20 lakh. It commenced at 7.5 per cent for properties valued at Rs 1 lakh. Property worth was determined based on market value at the time of the individual's demise. That was how it was in 1985 before it was abolished. As per many websites (I checked), the rupees has lost the value by 93% and ₹100 of 1985 is equivalent of ₹1540 or about that. That is 15.40 times. Let us make a clean 20 times. So ₹1 lakh (lower limit) is ₹20 lakh while ₹20 lakh (upper limit) is same as ₹4 Cr. Let me further curate these values. Let us say that this tax limit starts at ₹1 Cr at 5% and increases to 40% above ₹25 Cr. Straightaway, any proposed tax collection below 20% is not worthwhile. Then let me assume - tax starts at 20% at ₹4 Cr and reaches to 40% above ₹25 Cr. There will 4% education cess to pay. Still, do you see the problem? Every dead person’s heir will have to file tax returns to estimate the inheritance tax, the hassle, the fees paid to the lawyer to estimate the estate value, the fees to the CA who will prepare the returns, the time and energy spent, the value of your time, etc. Now let us look at affected party. The tax man is not going to differentiate with anyone. Assume that you inherit land or property that your grandfather acquired in the 50s. Assume that it is worth ₹10 Cr today. Easily possible, right? Let us further assume that you are the sole heir and inherit property and very little of liquid assets (money, gold, etc.). At 25% assumed tax rate, this will mean a tax of ₹2.5 Cr. Where will find this money? Remember that you are assumed to be an average middle-class 55-year old, whose father has just passed away. You have many big ticket expenses such as higher PG education of children (today ₹3 lakh/yr in India, ₹ 25 lakh/yr abroad min), their marriage expenses (today even a simple marriage costs upward of ₹8 lakhs), home expenses, providing for retirement (today it is ₹1.5 Cr for a retired couple) and many others. All these are only going to rise as per inflation. So will you have the ₹2.5 Cr to settle the inheritance tax? I can confidently say, “NO” as in all caps. Then how will you pay? You can do so only by selling your estate. After selling, you will have to pay the LTCG tax. Then from the balance you will have to pay the estate/inheritance tax. lest one forgets, there are emotions and memories associated with a property, especially ancestral property. Let us assume that you managed to pay tax without selling the property. Now when you die, your son/daughter will inherit your estate, including this ancestral property. The ancestral property will most likely be redeveloped and worth even more. You already paid the inheritance tax. But after your ultimate demise your heirs will have to pay the tax again. NOW, do you see how DRACONIAN this tax is? It is very easy to say that we will tax only the rich and others won’t be affected. The problem is that word “rich” is ambiguous without a quantum attached. It is also very easy to be swayed by the socialist/communist opinion - it looks good till it bites one’s own a$$. So …

Question: What makes metro rail a metro rail? Why can't Mumbai's and Chennai's existing extensive suburban line or Chennai's MRTS be called metro?
Answer: I don't think that any definition that separates suburban train system from metro rail system. The only technical difference can be that metro rail tracks are an independent system whereas suburban rail system is part of the greater long distance rail system. Now, after Delhi Metro, the other metro systems use standard gauge instead of broad gauge. But that is not the criterion.

Question: In Gujarat State of India, if the Cooperative housing society management gives No objection certificate to rent society home for running a doctor's office (commercial use of residential property) against the bylaws of the society, what is recourse?
Answer: As far as I know of residential property laws, a residential property such as bungalow, flat, etc, is allowed to be used for the purpose of some limited commercial activity. The following may explain: If you just go around the town and blocks, you will find plenty of such mini commercial establishments in a block of residential flats. But this is as far as I know. Please consult a lawyer on this. You may be able to stop the activity if you can prove that the activity is causing nuisance, parking problems, grave risk to security, etc. Then you may have a case. You may have to influence other members of the society supporting your case and then get a resolution passed in the AGM to not allow any commercial activity - small or large - by majority. Then it becomes an adopted resolution.

Name: Prasanna Bhalerao
Question: What is your review of Bharat Matrimony?
Answer: Generally speaking, people always write a review when the experience is bad. Very few people will write - so-and-so product/service was/is excellent; I am more than happy, etc. Why? This is because a good product or service is expected. This is just living up to the promise. It is very simple as that. If I buy a box of matchsticks, I expect them to light up when ignited. If half of the matchsticks don’t light up, the minimum that I will do is not buy the same brand again. So all in all, it is only expected that bad reviews are written on the social platform. I can see nothing but mostly bad to terrible reviews of Bharat Matrimony (BM) here. I am here to write my own experience. Like most, I don’t have any kind words. (Note that Bharat Matrimony is a sort of a parent and has many other affiliate sites such as Brahmin Matrimony, Tamil Matrimony, Kerala Matrimony, Marathi Matrimony and so on.) I signed up on BM for the sake of my son, for whom I am looking for a suitable match. So I registered. Then I paid for basic service and paid ₹4837 (incl. of 18% GST). I was looking for 2–3 days, i set the search criteria and all I found were profiles mostly without photos like this. Then two days later, an associate called me and said “Sir, with the basic membership you can only find obscure matches that do not meet/match your expectations. Many profiles are available under the premium package only. You should sign up for the premium package.” Then he said that the Premium Package is worth ₹11,000 something (can’t remember exactly) but he will apply a discount, also adjust some of the fee paid against the basic package and offer it to me for ₹5959 (incl GST). I agreed to that too and signed up. The basic package was for 6 months and the premium package was for 3 months. My experience for the next couple of months was none too good either. In the next couple of months. This is my PRIME membership: I received 3 connects and I sent 2 invites. Neither worked out. Now that is fine. I know that marriage is not something that will happen in an instant. Sometimes it may but it is a long-drawn process. But BM service leaves a lot to be desired. Now the Premium Package duration is nearly over, the people at BM have woken up. I received a call from an associate. This is what she had to say: Associate: Sir, I am ________. I noticed that your son has an excellent profile but you have not been able to find suitable matches as yet. I can help you. I work with you as a personal assistant, I can hunt more profiles, send them to you, connect both to each other, etc. etc. Me: What are your fees? Associate: Sir, the 3-month service fee is ₹24,nnn but I can offer the same to you for ₹16,nnn. Me: How will your service REALLY benefit me? Associate: Sir, as I said, I have access to the full database which you don’t. I will work exclusively on your son’s profile. I will select 2–3 profiles each week and send them to you. You can check them and if you like them go for further discussions. There too, I will help you coordinate the meeting. I will personally talk to them and to you and appraise both of the profiles, blah … blah … Me: If you say, you can hunt better, why don’t I see the profiles when I search? So far, in two months, with access every 2nd day, I have found 17 profiles only. Associate: Sir, you wouldn’t know how to search. I have deeper knowledge of how the website works … At this point, I rudely told her “Please … please … I am an IT veteran of 35 years. I have designed websites and written the backend — sometimes from scratch. Please do not patronize me thus. I have been on BM for over two months and I have not seen any benefit or value for my ₹10,000+. I am sorry to say that I do not take you at face value.” So ended the call on the first day. The next day, I received another call from the same person. She tried repeating the same story, the benefits of a personalized manager, etc. This time, I said, Me: Sorry. As I said yesterday, and pardon me again, I again say that I cannot take you at face value. I have an alternative. You work in a company and every year you must be undergoing an appraisal every year. I wish to appraise you as well. Associate: (she tried interrupting) … Me: Please do not interrupt. I was not finished. My proposal is this. You must work with me as you said you would but without me signing up for the special package. You will do so for a month. You must send me at least one profile a week (not even two) and I will evaluate your work. At the end of one month, if I am satisfied, I will sign up. Associate: (splutter, splutter) Sorry Sir. It does not work that way. Only after you sign up, your son’s profile is tagged to me. Then I have his complete information, biodata, etc. and I can work on matches. Me: Just now you said that you have access to the whole database. Now, you are telling me that my son’s profile is not accessible to you? No. That is not acceptable. Thank you for calling me. (I told her, my way or highway). So in a nutshell: (A copy of this post is being sent to that associate.)
